enzyme_name: L-threonylcarbamoyladenylate (TC-AMP) synthase, TsaC/Sua5
organism_context: Bacterial TsaC/YrdC; archaeal and eukaryotic Sua5 adds a C-terminal SUA5 domain with no demonstrated catalytic activity. A genuinely fused TsaD-TsaC-SUA5-TcdA module (TsaN) exists in pandoraviruses but is not the normal cellular catalyst.
rationale: TsaC/Sua5 carries a single catalytic activity, condensation of L-threonine, bicarbonate and ATP into TC-AMP (EC 2.7.7.87, KEGG K07566); the downstream transfer to tRNA is done by the separate TsaD/Kae1/Qri7 protein, and the extra SUA5 domain has no catalytic function.
direction_note: TC-AMP synthesis is pulled forward by PPi release and by immediate consumption of the labile TC-AMP by TsaD; no enzyme regenerates ATP from TC-AMP, so ModelSEED's reverse call has no enzymological basis.

enzyme_name: histidine N-alpha-methyltransferase (dimethylhistidine N-methyltransferase; EgtD in bacteria, methyltransferase domain of Egt1 in fungi)
distinct_activities: gamma-glutamyl-cysteine / cysteine sulfoxide synthase (non-heme iron C-S bond forming oxidase, EgtB-type activity)
organism_context: Fungi (Neurospora crassa Egt-1, Schizosaccharomyces pombe Egt1) fuse the sulfoxide synthase and the methyltransferase on one chain; Actinobacteria (Mycobacterium smegmatis/M. tuberculosis) split them into standalone, monofunctional EgtD and EgtB.
rationale: The methylation of N-alpha-methyl-L-histidine to N-alpha,N-alpha-dimethyl-L-histidine is step 2 of the three successive alpha-N-methylations that make hercynine; iterative methylation by one active site is a single activity, but in fungi this methyltransferase is fused to a genuine second catalytic domain (sulfoxide synthase), which is why this is scored bifunctional with the lineage recorded.
direction_note: SAM to SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible; the fused sulfoxide-synthase domain pulls hercynine onward into ergothioneine, reinforcing forward flux. KEGG flags R10524 as the middle step of a three-step methylation, but it is a real single-enzyme step, not a lump.

enzyme_name: unknown (janthitrem-cluster prenyltransferase/P450 steps, Jan/Ltm-type indole-diterpene enzymes)
organism_context: Penicillium janthinellum / Epichloe spp. epoxy-janthitrem indole-diterpene clusters
rationale: KEGG R10569 itself carries the COMMENT 'unclear reaction', has no EC or ortholog, and the ModelSEED entry is short by C10H12 (status MI:C:10/H:12); beta-paxitriol to janthitrem C requires several prenylation and oxygenation steps in the jan/ltm cluster, so no single enzyme catalyses it.
direction_note: Indole-diterpene biosynthesis elaborates the paxilline-type core toward the janthitrems, so the beta-paxitriol to janthitrem C sense is the biosynthetic one, but the KEGG entry is too poorly defined for a confident call.

enzyme_name: ADP-ribosyl cyclase / cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolase 1 (CD38); paralogue BST-1/CD157
distinct_activities: cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolase (cADPR + H2O -> ADP-ribose, EC 3.2.2.6) - this reaction
organism_context: Mammalian type II ectoenzyme CD38 and the GPI-anchored paralogue BST-1/CD157; the Aplysia homologue is cyclase-only.
rationale: A single polypeptide carries both the cyclase and the hydrolase activity, which is why KEGG ortholog K01242 lists EC 3.2.2.6 and 2.4.99.20 together; CD38 also runs NAD+ glycohydrolase and base-exchange chemistry at the same site.
direction_note: This is exactly a bifunctional enzyme whose two domains look like opposite reactions, but they are not: the hydrolase half is irreversible (cADPR + H2O -> ADPR), while the cyclase half makes cADPR from NAD+, not from ADP-ribose, so ModelSEED's reverse direction (ADPR -> cADPR + H2O) corresponds to no catalysed activity.

enzyme_name: A47934 sulfotransferase StaL (PAPS:desulfo-A47934 sulfotransferase)
organism_context: Streptomyces toyocaensis NRRL 15009, A47934 glycopeptide-antibiotic tailoring; homologues Teg12/Teg14 in other glycopeptide clusters
rationale: StaL is a single-domain cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase (EC 2.8.2.36) whose only activity is transfer of the sulfuryl group to the 4-hydroxyphenylglycine phenol of the A47934 aglycone; crystallography shows one PAPS site and one aglycone site.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way; desulfation back to desulfo-A47934 would require a sulfatase, a different enzyme.

enzyme_name: unknown (putative SAM-dependent methyltransferase of the MM 4550 / olivanic-acid carbapenem cluster acting on 'carbapenem biosynthesis intermediate 1', KEGG C20817)
organism_context: Streptomyces argenteolus ATCC 11009 (cmm cluster) / carbapenem biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG R10737 now returns HTTP 404, so the entry has been withdrawn upstream; the substrate is only labelled 'Carbapenem biosynthesis intermediate 1' and no gene from the cmm/MM 4550 cluster has been assigned to this methyl transfer, so the catalysing protein cannot be identified.
direction_note: Whatever methyltransferase runs it, SAM to SAH methyl transfer is thermodynamically one-way; the ModelSEED reverse direction would require SAH-dependent demethylation, which does not occur.

enzyme_name: putative PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase CmmSu (OA-6129 B1 sulfotransferase)
organism_context: Streptomyces argenteolus ATCC 11009, MM 4550 (olivanic acid) carbapenem cluster; KEGG ortholog K18571
rationale: Identity is inferred, not confirmed: KEGG R10751 explicitly calls this a 'putative PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase' that is 'not yet characterized sufficiently', and Li et al. only propose cmmSu as the sulfonating gene by bioinformatics and knockout phenotype; bacterial cytosolic sulfotransferases of this family are single-domain, hence monofunctional.
direction_note: PAPS-driven sulfuryl transfer runs forward; the reverse would be a sulfatase reaction catalysed by a different protein.

enzyme_name: unknown (spiro-lactonization to deoxynortryptoquialanone in the Penicillium aethiopicum tqa pathway; possibly spontaneous)
organism_context: Penicillium aethiopicum tryptoquialanine (tqa) gene cluster
rationale: MetaCyc RXN-16588 is the dehydrative closure of the ring-opened hydroxy-acid onto the 5-membered spirolactone of deoxynortryptoquialanone; Gao et al. assigned genes to the flanking NRPS and oxidative pyrazinone-opening steps but attached no protein to this cyclization, which may well be non-enzymatic.
direction_note: Pathway flux runs toward tryptoquialanine, whose spirolactone is present in the product, so the lactone-forming (water-releasing) direction is the physiological one.

enzyme_name: Mn(II)-oxidizing haem peroxidase MopA (animal-haem-peroxidase family)
organism_context: Erythrobacter sp. SD-21 MopA (requires haem and NAD+); Pseudomonas putida GB-1 MopA; distinct from the multicopper-oxidase Mn oxidases MnxG/MofA/CumA
rationale: EC 1.11.1.M1 is a MetaCyc-assigned placeholder for the peroxidase-type Mn(II) oxidase, best matched by the single-chain haem peroxidase MopA; no second catalytic activity is reported for it, and the Mnx-type Mn oxidase is a separate multi-subunit complex rather than a fused enzyme.
direction_note: The net equation collapses O2- and H2O2-driven oxidation of Mn(II) all the way to solid MnO2, i.e. the enzymatic Mn(II)->Mn(III) step plus largely abiotic disproportionation and precipitation, so no single enzyme catalyses it; regardless, Mn biomineralization is irreversible under oxic conditions and MnO2 reduction is a separate respiratory process.

enzyme_name: laccase (benzenediol:oxygen oxidoreductase, multicopper oxidase)
organism_context: Fungal and bacterial laccases; syringaldazine (4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxybenzaldehyde azine) to TMAMQ is the standard laccase activity assay
rationale: The EC 1.10.3.- assignment plus the syringaldazine/TMAMQ couple identifies this as a laccase; laccases are single-chain multicopper oxidases with one catalytic activity (one-electron phenol oxidation coupled to four-electron O2 reduction).
direction_note: Four-electron reduction of O2 to water at the trinuclear copper cluster makes laccase oxidation irreversible; the enzyme cannot re-reduce the quinoid TMAMQ product.

enzyme_name: glutathionyl-hydroquinone reductase (GS-HQR; PcpF / YqjG / Ecm4, Xi-class glutathione transferase)
organism_context: Sphingobium chlorophenolicum PcpF, Escherichia coli YqjG, Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ecm4, Phanerochaete chrysosporium GHR
rationale: GS-HQR (EC 1.8.5.7) is a single-domain Xi-class GST with one catalytic activity, GSH-dependent reductive removal of the glutathionyl group from glutathionyl-(hydro)quinones, proceeding through a mixed-disulfide intermediate on a single catalytic cysteine.
direction_note: The GSSG product has been dropped entirely (ModelSEED status MI:C:-20/H:-29/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2, i.e. two glutathiones' worth of atoms), so the group-contribution dG that drives ModelSEED's reverse call is computed on chemistry that is not the real reaction; the enzyme only runs deglutathionylation.

enzyme_name: peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase (transglycosylase domain of a class A penicillin-binding protein, e.g. PBP1a/PBP1b, PonA1/PonA2)
organism_context: Class A PBPs in most bacteria, including the mycobacterial PonA1/PonA2 of the quoted pathway, fuse both domains on one chain; monofunctional glycosyltransferases (MtgA/MGT) and the SEDS proteins RodA/FtsW carry the glycosyltransferase activity alone.
rationale: Textbook fused bifunctional enzyme: one polypeptide carries the N-terminal GT51 transglycosylase domain that polymerises lipid II (this reaction) and a C-terminal transpeptidase domain that cross-links the stem peptides.
direction_note: The glycan acceptor and the elongated product are both absent (status MI:C:-40/H:-62/N:-8/O:-21|CI:2), leaving lipid II -> undecaprenyl diphosphate with the sugar gone; in reality transglycosylation is driven by cleavage of the lipid II pyrophosphate and is irreversible, and neither PBP domain depolymerises glycan.

enzyme_name: sterol C-22 desaturase (cytochrome P450 CYP710 family; ERG5 in fungi)
organism_context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii and other green algae (7-dehydroporiferasterol branch); CYP710A in land plants, ERG5 in yeasts
rationale: The C-22(23) desaturation of 24-ethylcholesta-5,7-dien-3beta-ol is the CYP710/ERG5 sterol C-22 desaturase reaction, a single-activity P450; the NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase that feeds it electrons is a separate polypeptide, not a fused domain. Identity is inferred from the pathway rather than from a characterised algal protein, hence medium.
direction_note: The real reaction is an O2- and NADPH-consuming P450 desaturation (sterol + O2 + NADPH + H+ -> delta-22 sterol + 2 H2O + NADP+); ModelSEED instead writes the sterol handing a hydride to NADP+ with O2 and water dropped, which is what makes the gold-grade eQuilibrator value look near-isoergic and reversible. With O2 restored the reaction is strongly exergonic and one-way.

enzyme_name: 2,5-dichlorohydroquinone reductive dehalogenase LinD
organism_context: Sphingobium japonicum UT26 and other gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane (lindane) degraders
rationale: LinD is a single-domain GST-fold, glutathione-dependent reductive dehalogenase; it performs one catalytic activity, acting successively on 2,5-dichlorohydroquinone and then on chlorohydroquinone (same chemistry, different substrate, not a second activity).
direction_note: The GSSG product is missing (status MI:C:-20/H:-28/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2), so the thermodynamics ModelSEED used are not those of the real reaction; reductive dechlorination with chloride release is irreversible and LinD has no chlorinating activity.

enzyme_name: violaxanthin de-epoxidase (VDE)
organism_context: Plants and green algae (lumenal lipocalin-family enzyme); diatoms and Nannochloropsis use the related diadinoxanthin de-epoxidase
rationale: VDE carries one catalytic activity, ascorbate-dependent epoxide opening, which it applies twice in series (violaxanthin -> antheraxanthin -> zeaxanthin, the second half being this reaction); the opposite epoxidation is run by a completely separate enzyme, zeaxanthin epoxidase (ZEP).
direction_note: The xanthophyll cycle is two different enzymes pointing opposite ways: VDE does de-epoxidation (this entry, forward only, activated by low lumenal pH) and ZEP does the O2/NADPH-dependent epoxidation. ModelSEED's reverse direction therefore belongs to ZEP, not to this reaction; dehydroascorbate is also missing from the equation (status MI:C:-6/H:-7/O:-6).

enzyme_name: ADP-heptose:LPS heptosyltransferase I (WaaC / RfaC / HepI)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other Gram-negatives; LPS inner-core assembly (WaaF/HepII is the separate heptosyltransferase II)
rationale: WaaC is a single-domain GT-B glycosyltransferase that transfers L-glycero-D-manno-heptose from ADP-heptose to the inner Kdo of Kdo2-lipid A/IVA; it has one catalytic activity and the second heptose is added by a different gene product.
direction_note: The heptosylated Kdo2-lipid IVA product is absent entirely (status MI:C:-91/H:-159/N:-2/O:-43/P:-2|CI:7), leaving an entry that reads as two substrates giving only ADP + H+; glycosyl transfer from an ADP-sugar donor is irreversible in vivo, so the reverse call is an artefact of the broken equation.

enzyme_name: myo-inositol O-methyltransferase (IMT1; inositol 4-O-methyltransferase / myo-inositol 3-O-methyltransferase)
organism_context: Mesembryanthemum crystallinum IMT1 and orthologues in soybean and litchi (ononitol, pinitol and quebrachitol biosynthesis under osmotic stress)
rationale: IMT1 is a plant class-I SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase of the COMT family, a single-domain homodimeric enzyme with one catalytic activity; the homodimer is an oligomer, not a fused bifunctional chain.
direction_note: The methylated inositol product is missing (status MI:C:-7/H:-14/O:-6, i.e. C7H14O6 ononitol/bornesitol dropped); SAM-dependent O-methylation is irreversible and the methylinositol pool is an osmolyte sink, so flux is one-way forward.

enzyme_name: ATP-dependent sacrificial sulfur transferase LarE (carboxylate adenylation half-reaction)
organism_context: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum nickel-pincer nucleotide (P2TMN) cofactor biosynthesis for lactate racemase LarA
rationale: LarE is a single-domain PP-loop ATP pyrophosphatase with one overall activity: it adenylates a pyridinium carboxylate and then transfers sulfur from its own active-site cysteine, so the adenylation written here is a partial step of one mechanism, not an independent second activity.
direction_note: Adenylation with PPi release, followed by pyrophosphatase action and by irreversible sacrificial sulfur transfer, makes the forward direction effectively one-way in vivo.

enzyme_name: unknown (no single enzyme; strictosidine aglycone to catharanthine needs geissoschizine synthase, geissoschizine oxidase, Redox1/Redox2, precondylocarpine acetate synthase, dihydroprecondylocarpine acetate synthase and catharanthine synthase)
organism_context: Catharanthus roseus monoterpene indole alkaloid (MIA) pathway
rationale: This is a pathway-level summary, not an enzyme step: at least six characterised proteins stand between strictosidine aglycone and catharanthine, and the ModelSEED entry is also mass-unbalanced (status MI:H:-1/O:-2), so no catalysing enzyme can be named.
direction_note: MIA biosynthesis runs one way from strictosidine toward catharanthine, and none of the constituent steps operates in reverse, so ModelSEED's reverse recommendation is wrong even though the entry is a lump.

enzyme_name: pheophorbide a oxygenase (PAO; ACD1 / LLS1, Rieske-type iron-sulfur oxygenase) - this entry is the hydrolytic second half of the PAO reaction
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana ACD1 and maize LLS1; chlorophyll a degradation during senescence
rationale: PAO is the only enzyme implicated in the pheophorbide a -> red chlorophyll catabolite conversion and is a single-activity Rieske oxygenase (its ferredoxin electron donor and the downstream RCC reductase are separate proteins); the epoxypheophorbide intermediate of MetaCyc RXN-17253 is a mechanistic proposal and the ring-opening half may be spontaneous, so the catalyst of this isolated step is not established.
direction_note: Chlorophyll catabolism is a committed degradative flux and RCC is immediately consumed by RCC reductase, so only the forward direction occurs.

enzyme_name: unknown (exo-acting alpha-glucosidase / maltase implied by MetaCyc starch degradation II, but not identifiable from this entry)
organism_context: MetaCyc PWY-6724 starch degradation II
rationale: ModelSEED has reduced the entry to maltotriose <-> one glucose (status MI:C:-12/H:-20/O:-10, i.e. two glucose units and the waters dropped), leaving no usable chemistry; the pathway context implies an exo-acting alpha-glucosidase but no specific protein can be pinned to it.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is one-way under physiological conditions; resynthesising maltotriose from glucose would require a phosphorylase or transglycosylase, a different enzyme.

enzyme_name: dopamine beta-monooxygenase (dopamine beta-hydroxylase, DBH)
organism_context: Human/mammalian chromaffin granule and noradrenergic vesicle enzyme; amphetamine is a xenobiotic substrate hydroxylated to (-)-norephedrine (phenylpropanolamine)
rationale: DBH (EC 1.14.17.1) is a copper-dependent monooxygenase with one catalytic activity; it is a homo-oligomer (disulfide-linked dimer of dimers), which under the protocol is an oligomeric assembly, not a fused bifunctional chain. The amphetamine->norephedrine assignment follows the EC and the known DBH side-chain beta-hydroxylation of phenethylamines.
direction_note: Dehydroascorbate, the two-electron ascorbate product, is missing (status MI:C:-6/H:-7/O:-6); O2-dependent C-H hydroxylation is irreversible and nothing dehydroxylates norephedrine back to amphetamine.

enzyme_name: unknown (phylloquinone side-chain cleavage activity; the responsible protein has not been identified molecularly - UBIAD1 catalyses the opposite prenylation of menadione to MK-4)
organism_context: Mammalian intestine/tissues, menaquinone-4 biosynthesis from dietary vitamin K1 (MetaCyc PWY-7998)
rationale: Isotope-tracing work establishes that dietary phylloquinone is converted to menadione in vivo and then re-prenylated to MK-4 by UBIAD1, but the enzyme (if any) that removes the phytyl side chain has never been purified or cloned, so no catalyst can be named or classified.
direction_note: In vivo flux is cleavage (phylloquinone -> menadione + phytyl), and the only characterised enzyme in this part of the pathway, UBIAD1, uses geranylgeranyl-PP rather than phytol; ModelSEED's reverse direction (phytylation of menadione) is not a known reaction.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (non-enzymatic) aqueous decomposition of 4-hydroxybenzyl isothiocyanate
organism_context: Downstream of myrosinase action on sinalbin (4-hydroxybenzyl glucosinolate) in Sinapis alba and other Brassicales
rationale: 4-Hydroxybenzyl isothiocyanate is intrinsically unstable in water and breaks down to 4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol and thiocyanate without a catalyst, because the para-hydroxyl lets it ionise to a quinone-methide; no enzyme has been assigned to this step and MetaCyc carries it as a non-enzymatic conversion.
direction_note: Because the step is spontaneous and irreversible, no enzyme sets the direction; condensing thiocyanate with 4-hydroxybenzyl alcohol (ModelSEED's reverse) does not happen in cells.

enzyme_name: ferritin ferroxidase centre (H-type subunit; also bacterioferritin and mitochondrial ferritin FTMT)
organism_context: 24-meric ferritin cage; the catalytic di-iron site sits on the H-type subunit, L-chains are catalytically silent nucleation subunits
rationale: The stoichiometry (2 Fe2+ + O2 -> 2 Fe(III)-oxyhydroxide + H2O2) is the canonical H-chain ferroxidase/mineralisation reaction; ferritin's iron-storage role is a property of the assembled cage, not a second catalytic activity, and the 24-mer is a homo-oligomeric complex rather than a fused bifunctional chain.
direction_note: Ferroxidation and mineral-core growth are one-way; iron release from the core is a separate reductive/lysosomal process, not the reverse of this reaction.
